key_insight: A spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model uses weak lesion-mask supervision to make breast ultrasound predictions more interpretable and anatomically faithful.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve trust in AI-assisted breast ultrasound by aligning concept explanations with lesion regions and posterior acoustic effects that clinicians expect to matter.
method: Derive two weakly supervised zones from each lesion mask: an in-lesion region for morphology and a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena.
Train concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective to encourage concept evidence from the right anatomy.
Use a linear bottleneck classifier to preserve semantic faithfulness while supporting diagnosis.
evidence_signal: In five-fold stratified group cross-validation, SG-CBM improved diagnostic AUROC, concept macro-AUROC, and spatial alignment of concept evidence; a Train-corrupt/Test-clean test assessed sensitivity to annotation quality.
watch_item: The model’s trustworthiness depends on the quality of coarse lesion annotations, so noisy or inconsistent masks may weaken both explanation fidelity and diagnostic performance.
paper_title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
